correctness.rationale: Complete proof checks all possible cardinalities 0,1,2,3 of label-2 support at weight at most six. For two defenders the undominated cells are two cross corners or the remaining row/column cells. For three defenders all valid configurations are partial matchings or 2-by-2 elbows. These five disjoint families exhaust and attain all equality cases; counting them proves the formula. Explicit adjacency enumeration in verify.py independently matches 8 boards through 8-by-9. The finite computation is not presented as proof of the infinite theorem.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The known optimal weight is explicitly credited rather than claimed new. No identified general enumeration theorem of a stronger invariant specializes to the precise named Roman-optimum counting claim. Total Roman constraints are strictly stronger here (a three-defender elbow contains an isolated positive center), and Cartesian graph products are not tensor products.

arXiv:2005.13608v1 concerns the distinct total-Roman variant. An L triple has the elbow 2-vertex isolated in the induced positive support, so it is not total Roman despite being an ordinary Roman optimum.

arXiv:1908.02445v1 concerns ordinary set domination and total set domination, not Roman labels. The 2022 unitary-Cayley article retrieved by search classifies only rings whose Roman minimum is at most four; here the known minimum is six.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Knowing the minimum weight six gives no formula for the number or geometry of all assignments attaining it. None of the sources identified implies this enumerative refinement through specialization or a stronger uniform classification.

Closest mathematical-record results include Roman domination polynomials of complete multipartite graphs, a graph family not isomorphic to these direct clique products in the claimed range.

value.rationale: The theorem resolves the natural multiplicity and complete support geometry of all optimal Roman allocations on the two-parameter direct product family, refines a published minimum-six result, exposes exceptional width-four families, and proves almost-all asymptotic rigidity of optimal patterns. Unlike a routine formula substitution, it identifies five exhaustive combinatorial mechanisms and their exact contributions.
